content.title: About
content.content: Coconut water is the clear liquid found inside young green coconuts. The sweetened version contains added sugar or another sweetener, making it taste sweeter and more palatable. It is rich in electrolytes such as potassium, sodium, and magnesium, and is often used as a natural sports drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut water naturally contains fewer calories than most fruit juices.
Sweetened versions often use cane sugar or fruit syrup to preserve the coconut’s natural flavor.
It is considered a “natural” isotonic drink because of its high potassium content.
In some countries coconut water is sold as a concentrate that is diluted with water before consumption.
A single coconut palm can produce up to 50 liters of water per year.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: A rich electrolyte profile helps replenish fluids lost during exercise.

items.title: Heart support
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Coconut water contains virtually no fat, making it a light beverage.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: It provides vitamin C and small amounts of phenolic compounds that combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber can support regular bowel movements.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The sweetened version may contain significant added sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut products.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some commercial products can have elevated sodium, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coconut water can be enjoyed chilled as a refreshing drink, used in smoothies, cocktails, or in cooking as a substitute for water or fruit juice. The sweetened version is often served after workouts for quick energy replenishment.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened packages in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
